title: Data provider: Stooq (fallback)
description: Implement StooqProvider (app/data/stooq_provider.py) as the fallback market data source when yfinance fails or rate-limits, satisfying the same DataProvider protocol.

checklist.step: Implement get_daily_ohlcv(ticker) using Stooq's CSV endpoint, returning the same column shape as YFinanceProvider
Implement get_weekly_ohlcv(ticker) — resample daily bars to weekly since Stooq has no native weekly interval
Handle unknown ticker / insufficient history the same way as data-provider-yfinance (typed exceptions -> 404 / 422)
Write unit tests against recorded CSV fixtures — no live network calls
Confirm StooqProvider and YFinanceProvider are interchangeable behind the DataProvider protocol (shared contract test)
Run pytest --cov=app --cov-report=term-missing and confirm no regression

decisions.decision: Created app/data/exceptions.py on this branch with the exact same DataProviderError/TickerNotFoundError/InsufficientHistoryError/DataProviderUnavailableError hierarchy (same fields, same docstrings, same 404/422/503 mapping) as the one already implemented — but not yet merged to main — on task/data-provider-yfinance (PR #18), verified by reading that branch's actual file content directly (`git show origin/task/data-provider-yfinance:backend/app/data/exceptions.py`) rather than re-deriving the shape from scratch.
decisions.rationale: Per this task's own instructions, two options existed: (a) invent an independent minimal exception module now and reconcile later, or (b) read the real established convention off the not-yet-merged branch and match it exactly. Chose (b): since the content was directly verifiable (not fabricated) and the two tasks need identical semantics (same DataProvider protocol, same API-layer 404/422/503 mapping), matching verbatim means whichever of the two PRs merges second will find its own copy byte-for-identical to the other's and can simply keep either one / delete its own duplicate with a trivial no-op merge, rather than needing an actual reconciliation patch. Rejected: inventing a divergent shape now, which risks a real merge conflict or (worse) two subtly different exception hierarchies with the same names coexisting until someone notices.

decisions.decision: get_weekly_ohlcv resamples the daily series into Friday-ending weeks (`resample("W-FRI")`, open=first/high=max/low=min/close=last/volume=sum, dropping any bin with no trading days) rather than requesting Stooq's own `i=w` weekly interval param.
decisions.rationale: This task's own description and checklist explicitly state Stooq 'has no native weekly interval' and instruct resampling daily->weekly; followed that instruction as given rather than second-guessing it against outside knowledge of Stooq's URL API. W-FRI (week ending Friday) matches the standard trading-week convention (Mon-Fri) and keeps weekly bar boundaries stable regardless of which weekday `get_daily_ohlcv`'s underlying data happens to start/end on. The insufficient-history check (`_MIN_WEEKLY_BARS = 26`, docs/Analyse.md §8) is applied to the *resampled* weekly count, not the raw daily-bar count, mirroring YFinanceProvider's placement of the same check (verified via the same branch read as the exceptions.py decision above) so the two providers reject 'too little history' at the same effective threshold. Rejected: passing i=w to Stooq's endpoint directly (would contradict the explicit task instruction, and Stooq's real weekly CSV is known to have gaps/quirks around recent partial weeks that daily-bar resampling avoids); checking the 26-bar minimum on the daily count instead of the resampled weekly count (would need an independently-chosen daily threshold not stated anywhere in docs/Analyse.md — the same reasoning YFinanceProvider's task recorded for rejecting that option).

decisions.decision: Detect 'unknown ticker' by checking whether Stooq's CSV response body is the literal text 'No data' (Stooq's documented behavior for an invalid/delisted symbol — a plain-text body, not an HTTP error status), with a second belt-and-braces check for an empty/header-only parsed DataFrame in case the exact wording ever changes. A bare ticker like 'AAPL' is translated to Stooq's required `<symbol>.<market>` form by lowercasing and appending '.us' when no suffix is already present, assuming US equities as the default market (matching the implicit assumption YFinanceProvider's bare-ticker calls already make).
decisions.rationale: Per docs/architecture/Testing.md's no-live-network-calls rule, this couldn't be confirmed against a real Stooq response in this session; it's implemented against Stooq's documented/widely-observed CSV endpoint behavior, with the header-only-DataFrame fallback specifically so the exact wording of the 'no data' response isn't a single point of failure. The '.us' auto-suffix is necessary for Stooq's endpoint to resolve at all (its symbols aren't bare tickers) while keeping the DataProvider protocol's `ticker` argument itself provider-agnostic (a caller passes 'AAPL' the same way to either provider; only StooqProvider needs to know Stooq's own symbol format). Rejected: requiring callers to pass Stooq-formatted symbols directly, which would break the protocol's interchangeability guarantee (docs/architecture/Backend.md §2).

decisions.decision: The checklist's 'shared contract test proving StooqProvider and YFinanceProvider are interchangeable' is implemented in tests/unit/data/test_provider_contract.py scoped to StooqProvider alone for now (protocol-signature conformance + output-shape assertions), with YFinanceProvider deliberately left out of the `_PROVIDER_CLASSES` list and a comment + this decision recording it as a follow-up.
decisions.rationale: app/data/yfinance_provider.py on `main` is still the unimplemented stub (`raise NotImplementedError`) as of this task — data-provider-yfinance's real implementation only exists on its own not-yet-merged branch (PR #18) — so there is nothing real to compare Stooq's output against yet without reaching across branches into code this task doesn't own. Structuring the test as a parametrized list keyed by provider class means adding YFinanceProvider once it lands on `main` is a one-line change (append to `_PROVIDER_CLASSES`, add its own mocked-fetch fixture) rather than a rewrite. Rejected: skipping the contract test entirely until both providers exist, which would leave the DataProvider protocol's method-signature conformance completely unverified for Stooq in the meantime; importing/vendoring the yfinance branch's provider code into this branch to test against it now, which would create a fake dependency on unmerged, unreviewed code.

decisions.decision: Resolved the merge-conflict rebase against current `main` (which had since merged data-provider-yfinance's PR #18) by taking main's copy verbatim for both backend/app/data/exceptions.py (add/add conflict — only the docstring's cross-reference differed, pointing at data-provider-yfinance.json's decisions entry instead of this task's own) and backend/tests/unit/data/test_exceptions.py (add/add conflict — same docstring cross-reference plus the DataProviderUnavailableError 'plain message' test used a different example string, 'rate-limited' on main vs 'unreachable' on this branch), rather than keeping this branch's copies or hand-splicing the two. For docs/tasks/index.json's content conflict (both branches had flipped the same two data-provider-yfinance/data-provider-stooq lines in opposite directions, plus main had since flipped several unrelated already-merged tasks — indicator-stochastic, indicator-elder-ray, indicator-autoenvelope, screen1-tide, screen2-wave, confidence-scoring, portfolio-risk-rules — to done), kept main's state for every one of those already-merged tasks and set data-provider-yfinance to done (matching main, since PR #18 merged) and data-provider-stooq to implementing (this task's own true current state, not the stale 'planned' snapshot main had from before this branch existed).
decisions.rationale: The exceptions.py/test_exceptions.py divergence was purely cosmetic (an example string and a docstring's target-file reference), not a behavioral difference — the class hierarchy, fields, and 404/422/503 semantics were byte-identical, exactly as the original decision entry above anticipated ('whichever of the two PRs merges second will find its own copy byte-for-identical to the other's'). Since data-provider-yfinance's copy is the one that's already live on `main` and referenced by whatever else has landed since, keeping main's version outright (rather than this branch's, or a manual merge of the two docstrings) is the simplest resolution with zero behavioral risk and no orphaned cross-references. For index.json, the only lines this task has any authority over are its own and yfinance's (the pair both branches touched); every other flipped line reflects tasks that genuinely merged to main after this branch was cut, so keeping main's value for those is just accepting reality, not a judgment call. Full backend suite re-run post-merge: 242 passed, 95.65% coverage (app/data/exceptions.py and app/data/stooq_provider.py both 100%), confirming the merge introduced no regression. Rejected: keeping this branch's stale exceptions.py/test copy (would silently diverge the two providers' typed-exception source of truth, defeating the whole point of the original decision to match verbatim); hand-merging both docstrings into a single conjoined reference (unnecessary complexity for a purely cosmetic difference).

comments.summary: exceptions.py provenance claim independently verified: diffed against origin/task/data-provider-yfinance's copy, identical except a 4-line docstring pointing at this task's own decisions entry instead of the yfinance task's — a cosmetic, expected difference, not a functional divergence.

Minor correctness edge case (non-blocking): _to_stooq_symbol treats any '.' in the ticker as an existing market suffix, so a literal dotted class-share ticker like 'BRK.B' would skip the '.us' suffix and produce the wrong Stooq symbol (Stooq/yfinance both use a hyphen for class shares, e.g. brk-b.us). Low impact since this app's own ticker convention already uses hyphens, so it only bites on non-canonical input. Worth a follow-up fix + test.
Nit (non-blocking): unused `import urllib.error` — all transport failures go through the broad `except Exception` in _fetch_daily, never a specific urllib.error type. Dead code.

Minor doc gap (non-blocking): docs/architecture/Backend.md §2's module-layout diagram doesn't list app/data/exceptions.py. The module's existence is well-justified and recorded in this task's decisions, just not reflected in the architecture doc's diagram yet — suggest a small follow-up once the exceptions.py duplication with PR #18 (data-provider-yfinance) is reconciled.

OVERRIDE (pr-decision, blocking): the exceptions.py duplication with PR #18 flagged above as a cosmetic non-issue is no longer cosmetic now that #18 actually merged to main (2026-09-15, after this review). `gh pr view 19 --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus` now reports CONFLICTING/DIRTY. Reproduced locally: merging origin/main into this branch produces real add/add conflicts in backend/app/data/exceptions.py (differing docstring) and backend/tests/unit/data/test_exceptions.py (differing DataProviderUnavailableError message fixture: 'unreachable' vs 'rate-limited', not just the docstring), plus a content conflict in docs/tasks/index.json (both branches flip the same two task-state lines in opposite directions, since yfinance's own task now shows done on main but this branch still has it as planned). None of this is architecturally hard to resolve, but it does require an actual code change (picking/merging the exceptions.py and test content, fixing index.json) that pr-decision is not permitted to make itself — GitHub itself will refuse gh pr merge as-is.
